title: State v. Franklin
questions: Whether the trial court in a prosecution for cyberstalking erroneously disallowed evidence that someone else committed the crime after allowing the alleged other suspect to assert her Fifth Amendment right to remain silent.

title: Sargent v. Seattle Police Department
questions: Whether the exemption from the Public Records Act for law enforcement investigative records expired when the underlying case was referred for prosecution, and if so, whether the law enforcement agency was thereafter required to comply with the original public records request.

title: State v. Clark
questions: Whether nontribal police officers were required to obtain a search warrant from a tribal court in order to search the home of a tribal member located on tribal land for evidence of a crime committed on fee land within the boundaries of an Indian reservation.

title: King County v. King County
questions: Whether a materials processing facility was a valid nonconforming use even though it was established in part by nonpermitted clearing and grading.

title: State v. Dobbs
questions: Whether in a prosecution for domestic violence offenses the defendant’s conduct toward the victim before and after his arrest supported a ruling that he forfeited his right to challenge the admission of the unavailable victim’s out-of-court statements, even though there was no evidence that the defendant threatened the victim not to testify or direct evidence that the victim refused to appear because of threats.

title: Columbia Community Bank v. Newman Park
questions: Whether a subsequent “volunteer” lender foreclosing on a deed of trust may be equitably subrogated to a previous loan encumbering the real property.

title: Cedar River Water & Sewer District v. King County
questions: Whether Snohomish County’s approval of community mitigation projects related to a sewage treatment facility was a land use decision subject to the time limit on judicial challenges under the Land Use Petition Act.

title: In re Personal Restraint Petition of Stockwell
questions: Whether a personal restraint petitioner alleging that his guilty plea was involuntary because he was misinformed of the maximum sentence must establish actual and substantial prejudice in order to obtain relief.

title: In re the Estate of Virgil Becker
questions: Whether the spouse of a decedent, who is not a beneficiary under the will, had standing to intervene in a will contest in order to challenge a settlement between the will challengers and the guardian ad litem of the surviving spouse’s minor child, the sole beneficiary under the will.

title: Raven v. Department of Social & Health Services
questions: Whether in an action for neglect of a ward under the abuse of vulnerable adults act, chapter 74.34 RCW, the State need only prove the guardian engaged in a pattern of conduct resulting in a deprivation of care, not that the conduct caused the ward harm or that the ward would have accepted an alternative care plan had one been offered.

title: Kofmehl v. Baseline Lake
questions: Whether a seller who claims to be ready, willing, and able to perform a real estate sales contract that violates the statute of frauds may avoid the remedy of restitution of the earnest money if the parties disagree as to the terms of the contract, and if so, whether the buyer bears the burden of proving that the seller is not ready, willing, and able to perform.

title: Dean v. Fishing Company of Alaska
questions: Whether in a Jones Act case brought by a maritime worker the trial court correctly applied the summary judgment standard to the worker’s pretrial motion to reinstate maintenance and cure.

title: Stewart Title Guaranty v. Sterling Savings Bank
questions: Whether equitable subrogation was available to a bank on the basis of a construction and purchase loan to a developer intended to pay off existing liens on the property, giving the bank priority over a subsequent mechanic’s lien.

title: Youngs v. PeaceHealth
questions: Whether under Louden v. Myhre, 110 Wn.2d 675, 756 P.2d 128 (1988), attorneys representing a defendant hospital corporation in a medical malpractice action are prohibited from having ex parte contact with nonparty treating physicians employed by the hospital corporation, and if so, whether Louden was abrogated by amendments to RCW 5.60.060(4) providing that the waiver of the physician-patient privilege for any one physician following the filing of a medical malpractice lawsuit constitutes a waiver of the privilege as to all physicians.

title: International Marine Underwriters v. ABCD Marine, LLC
questions: Synopsis: Whether a partner in a general partnership qualifies as a third party to an indemnification agreement between the partnership and another business bringing the personal injuries he suffered while on the job within the coverage provided by the partnership's comprehensive general liability insurance policy.

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Haghighi
questions: The trial court admitted evidence at Mr. Haghighi's trial under the inevitable discovery doctrine. After Mr. Haghighi's judgment was final, this court rejected the use of the inevitable discovery doctrine in another case. This court must decide whether that case applies retroactively to Mr. Haghighi's judgment.

title: Freeman v. State
questions: Does the State's lease of a portion of I-90 to Sound Transit violate article II, section 40 of the Washington Constitution and RCW 47.12.120?

title: McKown v. Simon Prop. Group Inc.
questions: Whether, in this action brought against a mall owner and a mall security firm by a store employee who was one of those shot during a third party’s criminal rampage, the plaintiff must show that similar violent acts previously occurred on the premises in order to establish that the defendants owed him a duty to protect him from the third party’s criminal acts.

title: State v. Sanchez
questions: Whether, in light of a 2011 amendment to RCW 7.09.345 that requires the end-of-sentence review committee to assign risk levels to sex offenders (Laws of 2011, ch. 338, Â§ 5), a juvenile court was nonetheless required by RCW 4.24.550(6) to transmit a juvenile offender’s Special Sex Offender Disposition Alternative evaluation to the county sheriff for risk classification.

title: In re Starczewski, Attorney at Law
questions: Was Starczewski's disciplinary hearing fair and proper, and should the Disciplinary Board’s penalties be affirmed?

title: Brown v. MHN Government Services, Inc.
questions: Whether a mandatory arbitration clause in a contract between social service professionals and a corporation that provides social and counseling services to members of the military is unconscionable.

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Gomez
questions: Whether the defendant in a prosecution for homicide by abuse and first degree manslaughter was deprived of effective assistance of counsel due to counsel’s inexperience, mishandling of expert testimony, and lack of preparation and administrative support.

title: Jafar v. Webb
questions: Whether a superior court, upon finding a litigant indigent in connection with an application to waive filing fees and surcharges under General Rule 34, must waive all fees and surcharges or may grant a partial waiver.

title: In re Wickersham, Attorney at Law
questions: The court reviews findings of misconduct against an attorney and decides whether to impose a three-year suspension.

title: State v. Johnson
questions: Johnson appealed his conviction for driving while license suspended in the third degree (DWLS), claiming that the DWLS law does not criminalize driving with a license suspended for failing to pay traffic fines. He also argued that the State could not constitutionally suspend his license because of his indigence. Finally, he contended that the State must pay the costs of his appeal.

title: Wilkinson v. Chiwawa Communities Association
questions: Whether a homeowners association properly amended its covenants to prohibit the short-term rental of homes in light of existing covenants limiting use to single family residences and prohibiting commercial use of properties.

title: State v. Vasquez
questions: Whether a defendant’s possession of forged documents without evidence that the defendant used the documents for any purpose supports an inference of intent to defraud sufficient to convict the defendant of forgery.

title: In re Sanai, Attorney at Law
questions: Sanai was disbarred following a disciplinary process; did this process violate Sanai's constitutional rights?

title: King County Public Hospital No. 2 v. Washington State Department of Health
questions: Whether the Department of Health properly issued a certificate of need in settlement of an adjudicative hearing on the validity of the department’s original decision denying a certificate, and whether in doing so it properly relied on data collected after the original decision.

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Lain
questions: Whether the governor’s power under RCW 9.95.160 to “cancel or revoke” an offender’s probation authorizes the governor to overrule a decision of the Indeterminate Sentence Review Board granting probation, and if so, whether the offender is entitled to due process protections.

title: State v. Hinton
questions: Did police violate the defendant's constitutionally protected right to privacy when, without a warrant, they observed and responded to the defendant's text messages which appeared on the screen of a third party's wireless device?

title: State v. Roden
questions: Does a person have a privacy interest in a text message once it is sent?

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Adams
questions: A trial court sentenced Devon Adams in 2000 for first degree murder and unlawful possession of a firearm. Adams claims that because he was re-sentenced in 2009, he should now be able to raise an ineffectiveness of trial counsel claim

title: State v. Lynch
questions: In a second degree rape case, did the trial court violate Lynch's constitutional rights when it instructed the jury that Lynch had the burden of proving consent?

title: Ockletree v. Franciscan Health Sys.
questions: Does the exemption for nonprofit religious employers from Washington's law against discrimination violate the state constitution?

title: State v. Mau
questions: A jury found that the petitioner presented false information to the claims adjuster for a self-insured rental truck company. In doing so, did she commit the crime of presenting a false claim "for payment of a loss under a contract of insurance?"

title: State v. McEnroe
questions: Whether the State violates Washington statutes and a defendant's rights to equal protection under the law when, in deciding whether to file a notice to seek the death penalty, the State considers the strength of the evidence of the defendant's guilt in addition to the sufficiency of any mitigating circumstances

title: Rekhter v. Dep't of Soc. & Health Servs.
questions: The Department of Social and Health Services challenges a judgment of more than $90 million after a jury found that the agency breached its contractual duty of good faith and fair dealing toward in-home care providers

title: State v. Chen
questions: Whether the trial court erred in refusing to seal the defendant's competency evaluation in light of RCW 10.77.210, which limits disclosure of competency evaluations.

title: Fisher Broad. v. City of Seattle
questions: The Seattle Police Department records many of its contacts with people. Did it violate the Public Records Act when it told a reporter that it did not have a list of recordings and would not release the recordings?

title: NANETTE AURDAL, et ux v. UNITED TELEPHONE COMPANY OF THE NORTHWEST, dba SPRINT
questions: Can Burnston argue on appeal that the hit-and-run statute does not apply to collisions with a horse? Does it?

title: Cost Mgmt. Servs. v. City of Lakewood
questions: Cost Management Services (CMS) asked the City of Lakewood for a refund of taxes. Lakewood issued a demand to CMS for payment of taxes that did not mention the refund request. Was CMS required to exhaust its administrative remedies in Lakewood before bringing a case in state court for its refund claim?

title: Schroeder v. Weighall
questions: Whether RCW 4.16.190(2), which eliminates tolling for minors' medical malpractice claims, violates article I, sections 10 and 12 of the Washington Constitution, and the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution.

title: State v. Dye
questions: Does it violate a defendant's fair trial rights for the developmentally disabled victim to have a facility dog present during his testimony

title: Hill v. Garda CL Nw. Inc.
questions: The court considers issues stemming from a trial court's order to compel class arbitration in a labor dispute.

title: State v. Wooten
questions: Can a defendant be convicted of malicious mischief for damaging a house he was purchasing on a real estate contract?

title: Frizzell v. Murray
questions: Whether the grantor of a deed of trust waived her right to assert post sale challenges following a trustee's non-judicial foreclosure sale when she failed to enjoin the sale

title: PT Air Watchers v. Dep't of Ecology
questions: Whether the Department of Ecology, in determining that no environmental impact statement was necessary for a proposed project, failed to adequately consider the effects of carbon dioxide emissions and demand for woody biomass, and whether the project is exempt from the environmental impact statement requirement as part of an energy recovery facility that existed before January 1, 1989

title: State v. Zillyette
questions: Is an information charging a defendant with controlled substances homicide valid when it fails to specify what drug killed the victim?

title: Cornelius v. Dep't of Ecology
questions: Whether the Pollution Control Hearings Board correctly determined that the Department of Ecology did not violate the Washington Constitution or Revised Code when it approved Washington State University's applications to amend the water rights serving the Pullman campus

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Brockie
questions: Benjamin Brockie challenges his robbery and kidnapping convictions because the jury was instructed on a means of committing robbery that was not described in the charges against him.

title: State v. Bao Dinh Dang
questions: Must a trial court find persons acquitted by reason of insanity dangerous before revoking their conditional release from commitment, and, if so, under what standard of proof? In addition, was the trial court's admission of hearsay evidence at the hearing to revoke Dang's conditional release reversible error?

title: AllianceOne Receivables Mgmt., Inc. v. Lewis
questions: When a plaintiff files a lawsuit for damages of $10,000 or less, and later voluntarily dismisses the suit, is the defendant entitled to attorney fees and costs as the prevailing party?

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against McGrath
questions: The court reviews findings of misconduct against an attorney and decides whether to disbar him

title: In Re Marriage of Buecking
questions: Does the 90 day waiting period for a dissolution decree begin with the filing of a petition for legal separation and, if not, does a court have jurisdiction to enter a decree before 90 days have elapsed?

title: Jones v. City of Seattle
questions: A jury awarded the plaintiff $12.75 million for injuries that her brother, Mark, sustained as a result of the City's negligence. The City seeks a new trial on damages, arguing that it has surveillance video proving that Mark is not as injured as he claimed to be. Did the trial judge abuse her discretion when she excluded three of the City's witnesses because they were disclosed after trial had already started, or when she denied the City's motion for a new trial because she found it had not exercised "reasonable diligence" in investigating Mark's physical condition?

title: Hundtofte v. Encarnacion
questions: May a trial judge order the clerk to replace someone's name with initials in an electronic court docket? If so, when?

title: In re Parentage of C.M.F.
questions: Whether a parentage order is a custody decree that a court cannot change without following the statutory requirements, found in RCW 26.09.260 and .270, for modification.

title: Washburn v. City of Federal Way
questions: Can the court consider the City of Federal Way's arguments that it is not liable for the death of Baerbel K. Roznowski? If so, is the City liable?

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Gentry
questions: The court considers a death-row inmate's claim that his trial was prejudiced by prosecutorial misconduct

title: State v. Piatnitsky
questions: When a suspect under custodial interrogation tells police "I don't want to talk right now, man," 1) is the suspect more protected under the state constitution than under the federal constitution, and 2) is the suspect's statement an unequivocal invocation of his right to remain silent?

title: Friends of Columbia Gorge, Inc. v. State Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council
questions: Whether the Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council and Governor properly granted approval for the Whistling Ridge Wind Energy Project?

title: State v. Monfort
questions: May a county prosecutor consider the facts of the crime when determining whether to seek the death penalty? And, did the county prosecutor in this case consider sufficient mitigating circumstances when determining whether to seek the death penalty?

title: Eubanks v. Brown
questions: Must sexual harassment claims against a deputy prosecutor be tried in the county where the harassment occurred?

title: State v. Jordan
questions: The court considers whether a sentencing court erred in finding that a manslaughter conviction from Texas was legally comparable to a manslaughter conviction from Washington for the purposes of calculating an offender score

title: State v. Deskins
questions: After the defendant was convicted of confining dogs in an unsafe manner, did the trial court have authority to order the defendant to forfeit all of her pets and livestock, pay $21,582 in restitution to the sheriff's office, and live away from all pets and livestock during her two year probationary period?

title: State v. Gower
questions: Gower was convicted of incest and indecent liberties at a bench trial. Based on a statute that has since been found unconstitutional, the trial judge admitted evidence of Gower's prior sex crimes. Was that reversible error?

title: State v. Humphries
questions: Did the trial court err in allowing the defense attorney to stipulate to an element of the charged crime over the objection of the defendant?

title: State v. Pena Fuentes
questions: After the defendant's conviction but while a motion for a new trial was pending, a detective listened to phone conversations between the defendant and his attorney. Should the defendant's criminal charges be dismissed with prejudice?

title: Ellensburg Cement Prods., Inc. v. Kittitas County
questions: The court must decide: (1) whether Kittitas County's procedure for appealing environmental determinations violated state law; and (2) whether a county board correctly interpreted the county's zoning ordinances to permit gravel processing on agricultural land

title: State v. Garcia
questions: The petitioner asks the court to review the elements of kidnapping in the first degree. He also asks the court to consider whether there was sufficient evidence to sustain a kidnapping conviction, whether his right to present a defense was violated, and whether there was prosecutorial misconduct at trial.

title: In re Det. of Morgan
questions: The court considers whether an accused sexually violent predator (SVP) has a due process right to be competent during an SVP commitment trial, and whether an in-chambers discussion regarding an order to involuntary medicate the petitioner violated his article I, section 10 right to a public trial

title: State v. K.L.B.
questions: The court must decide: (1) whether a Sound Transit Fare Enforcement Officer whose employment is contracted through a private security firm is a "public servant," and (2) whether the definition of "public servant" is unconstitutionally vague

title: State v. Coley
questions: Did the trial court err in placing the burden of proof on competency after an initial finding of incompetency and what is the remedy if the burden is misallocated? Was the defendant denied his right to self-representation?

title: State v. Kipp
questions: Did the trial court err in admitting into evidence a secretly recorded conversation between Kipp and his brother-in-law in violation of the privacy act?

title: State v. MacDicken
questions: When police arrested Abraham MacDicken, they moved the stolen bags he was carrying a car's length away and searched them without a warrant. Were the bags too far away for the search to be valid? Can MacDicken challenge a search of stolen property?

title: LK Operating, LLC v. Collection Grp., LLC
questions: Were any attorney ethical rules violated in the formation of a joint business venture agreement, and what are the consequences if they were?

title: LK Operating, LLC v. Collection Grp., LLC
questions: In a legal malpractice case, has the complaining party shown that it suffered any damages?

title: Jametsky v. Olsen
questions: Washington law protects the owners of distressed properties. The issue before the court is whether a county treasurer must start the tax foreclosure process before a property can be considered distressed because of nonpayment of taxes

title: State v. Koss
questions: The court must decide whether a discussion in private between the judge and counsel about jury instructions violated the defendant's right to a public trial

title: State v. Smith
questions: The trial court held sidebar conferences on objections to evidence in a hallway outside the courtroom. This court must decide whether these conferences violated Mr. Smith's right to a public trial.

title: In re Estate of Toland
questions: Whether a Japanese divorce decree should be registered under the doctrine of comity

title: State v. Shearer
questions: During each of the defendants' criminal trials, one potential juror was questioned in the judge's chambers. Did this violate the constitutional right to a public trial?

title: State v. Njonge
questions: The court considers several questions connected to Njonge's claim that his right to a public trial was violated.

title: State v. Slert
questions: The Washington State Constitution requires open public trials. Was the constitution violated when four potential jurors were dismissed after an in-chambers review of their answers to a jury questionnaire?

title: State v. Frawley
questions: Can a defendant waive his public trial right under the Washington State Constitution?

title: Kumar v. Gate Gourmet, Inc.
questions: Does Washington's Law Against Discrimination require employers to make reasonable accommodations for an employee's religious practices?

title: State v. Witherspoon
questions: Mr. Witherspoon challenges his robbery conviction and Persistent Offender Accountability Act sentence of life in prison without the possibility of release.

title: Gray v. Suttell & Assocs.
questions: The United States District Court for the Eastern District of Washington certified the following question to us: Does the pre-2013 definition of "collection agency" in Washington's Collection Agency Act include debt buyers?

title: Wash. Educ. Ass'n v. Dep't of Ret. Sys.
questions: Could the State Legislature lawfully eliminate investment fund "gain-sharing" from some public pension plans?

title: Washington Education Association, Et Al. v. Washington Department of Retirement Systems
questions: The Uniform Cost of Living Adjustment (UCOLA) added an extra sum onto each state retiree's monthly pension payment to account for changes in cost of living and increased inflation. This court considers whether the repeal provisions of UCOLA unconstitutionally impaired the state's contract with its employees.

title: Town of Woodway v. Snohomish County
questions: The court considers whether a developer has the vested right to have its permit applications processed under land use ordinances that were found not to comply with the State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA) after the developer submitted its complete applications

title: Anaya Gomez v. Sauerwein
questions: The court decides whether a patient can sue a health care provider under Washington's informed consent law for not informing the patient about a lab test result that the provider mistakenly believed was a false positive.

title: Ralph v. Dep't of Natural Res.
questions: The court considers whether tort actions seeking monetary damages for injuries to real property fall within the scope of RCW 4.12.010 and, if so, whether the statute's filing requirements relate to jurisdiction or venue

title: State v. Jones
questions: This case involves whether Leroy Jones's Florida convictions are comparable to a Washington "most serious offense" under the Sentencing Reform Act and whether defense counsel was ineffective when it failed to investigate two witnesses

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Petersen
questions: This case asks whether the Certified Professional Guardianship Board can discipline Lori Petersen for her decisions made on behalf of three of her wards

title: In re Pers. Restraint of McNeil
questions: Should the Petitioners' sentences for murders they committed as juveniles be changed based on the recent U.S. Supreme Court case of Miller v. Alabama?
